exemplars.what_makes_it_premium: Entrance choreography doubles as a tutorial: the world pops up from the ground and the car drops with a physics bounce plus a paper-unwrap sound, demonstrating 'you can drive and knock things over' in the first second without any text. Zero real-time lights — matcap shading, shadows baked in Blender to PNG-8, light bounce faked by dot(normal, up) scaled by distance-to-ground, dynamic shadows are opacity-animated planes under moving objects. Camera is a damped follow-cam (eased lerp, never parented) that conveys speed; in the projects zone it tweens overhead. Sound design via Howler.js: collision SFX pick randomly from several similar files, volume scaled by impact velocity, playback rate randomized so nothing repeats identically; engine pitch tracks acceleration. Springy secondary motion (antenna recoils against acceleration). 2.8 MB total site weight via Draco (50-70% model reduction); mobile gets a purpose-built joystick + direction buttons instead of a broken desktop scheme. Case study: https://medium.com/@bruno_simon/bruno-simon-portfolio-case-study-960402cc259b

One committed concept executed to the pixel: a 3D desk with a CRT whose screen is a REAL working OS — a separate 2D React app served in an iframe and composited into the scene via CSS3DRenderer, so you genuinely type and click inside the 3D monitor. Custom GLSL post stack sells the CRT: screen curvature, scanlines/interlacing, chromatic aberration, flicker and bloom around the phosphor. The loader is diegetic — a BIOS/boot sequence themed as the machine powering on, so waiting is part of the fiction. Camera does authored dolly-in/dolly-out between room view and screen view with smooth focus shifts; ambient hum and mechanical keyboard audio complete the illusion. Built React + Three.js + TypeScript with ~3.4% of the codebase as GLSL (repos: github.com/henryjeff/portfolio-website).

exemplars.site: Jesse Zhou — Jesse's Ramen (cyberpunk ramen shop)
exemplars.what_makes_it_premium: The 'pre-rendered quality in a browser' trick: every light and shadow baked in Blender ray tracing into textures, so the runtime scene has no lighting cost and looks like an offline render. Neon comes from bloom post-processing (originally a selective dual-pass composite); floor reflections use three.js Reflector rendered at reduced resolution and opacity to stay cheap. Camera navigation is hardcoded GSAP tweens of position + target simultaneously between points of interest, with OrbitControls disabled during transit and re-enabled on arrival — no free-flight jank. In-scene UI screens are Photoshop-designed static textures with invisible raycast hitboxes, so 'buttons' in 3D are pixel-perfect art. Runtime device benchmark at load tiers the experience — disables reflections, pauses video textures, kills bloom, swaps in matcaps — to hold ~45fps. Case study: https://jesse-zhou.medium.com/jesses-ramen-case-study-77bae77ab5f0

Awwwards SOTD + Developer Award (Oct 2025). A multiplayer cyberpunk world where visitors see each other while browsing work — presence as a feature. Custom WebGPU renderer (he is the engineer who contributed VAO optimizations Bruno used) hits 120+ fps; Vue orchestrates UI state and GSAP drives transitions. Navigation is spatial — each 'room' is a project — but movement between rooms is authored, so exploration never degrades into aimless orbiting. Shows the current ceiling: WebGPU-first with graceful WebGL fallback.

FWA Site of the Day (Oct 2025). Premium feel comes from ambient density: grass swaying, a waterfall, fire, wind, butterflies — dozens of small idle animations so the scene is alive even when the user does nothing. Camera moves point-to-point between fixed, art-directed vantage points rather than free orbit, so every frame the user can reach is a composed shot; the island is discoverable from all angles but only through curated positions.

Awwwards SOTD. Solves the 'open world with no direction' problem with a guided protagonist: a cyclist rides a course through the 3D island and the camera follows him, surfacing each portfolio section as he passes it — narrative sequencing instead of a free camera. Click-and-drag scrubs progress along the path, which means input maps to a single authored timeline (like scroll) rather than 6-DOF chaos, so it cannot be broken by the user.

exemplars.site: Lusion v3 (studio site — the craft ceiling for interactive 3D)
exemplars.what_makes_it_premium: Awwwards/FWA/CSSDA Site of the Year. Master class in 'precompute offline, play back in real time': cloth simulation pre-calculated in 3 directions and stored in two PNG textures (positions + normals) as vertex animation textures; translucent hero objects fake subsurface scattering by combining pre-rendered normal/AO/thickness/diffuse maps with matcaps; big-screen scenes are Redshift offline renders whose camera path was exported to JSON so the real-time GLTF layer (150 KB) syncs perfectly with the video. Nothing expensive is computed live. Case study: https://www.awwwards.com/case-study-for-lusion-by-lusion-winner-of-site-of-the-month-may.html

The template for the 'cozy room' genre everyone copies (multiple discourse clones cite it). Everything baked: Blender-modeled room exported as .glb with all lighting/shadow baked to UV textures; screens in the scene run custom GLSL animations instead of video files; a day/night theme toggle swaps baked texture sets with a smooth shader crossfade. Its premium quality is restraint — soft palette, one interaction idea, zero performance strain.

craft_principles: Loading is Act One, not a spinner: tie a percentage counter to real asset progress (THREE.LoadingManager / drei useProgress), lerp the displayed number toward actual progress so it never jumps in chunks or stalls at 99, then gate entry behind a click ('Start' / 'Enter') — the click both creates an entrance beat and satisfies browser autoplay policy so your AudioContext can start. Best-in-class loaders are diegetic (Henry Heffernan's BIOS boot sequence IS the loading screen).

Entrance choreography teaches the interaction model wordlessly: Bruno Simon's world pops from the ground and the car falls with a physics bounce + sound, proving 'this is a physical toy' in one second. Stage the scene assembling (staggered scale/position tweens with back.out or elastic easing) rather than fading in a finished frame.

Camera rig hierarchy (pick one, never raw defaults): (a) authored point-to-point — GSAP-tween camera.position and controls.target simultaneously (power2/power3.inOut, ~1.2-2s), disable controls during transit, re-enable on arrival (Jesse Zhou, Jordan Breton); (b) damped follow-cam — exponential damping (THREE.MathUtils.damp, lambda ~3-5) toward the target each frame, never hard-parented, which conveys speed (Bruno); (c) path-scrub — input maps to progress along one authored spline (Joshua's World), unbreakable by the user. If you must allow orbiting, clamp minPolarAngle/maxPolarAngle, minDistance/maxDistance, disable pan, enableDamping with dampingFactor ~0.05. Add subtle cursor parallax (damped +-2-3 degree camera offset from normalized mouse) for idle life.

Postprocessing stack: R3F defaults to ACESFilmicToneMapping — keep it (or AgX for less orange skew), and put the ToneMapping pass LAST in the EffectComposer. For bloom, set luminanceThreshold above 1.0 (e.g. 1.1) so only genuinely HDR/emissive pixels (emissiveIntensity > 1 materials) glow instead of washing the whole frame. A lean premium stack is Bloom + Vignette + subtle ChromaticAberration + N8AO; set Canvas gl props antialias:false/stencil:false when the composer handles AA (SMAA). Effects must serve the concept — Henry's CRT curvature/scanlines exist because the site IS a CRT; Bruno only blurs the screen edges.

Bake everything, light nothing: pre-render lighting in Blender Cycles onto UV-mapped textures (Jesse Zhou, bokoko33) or use matcaps (Bruno — zero lights in the entire scene) or a single environment map (drei Environment with ground projection) instead of punctual lights + shadow maps. Fake dynamic shadows with opacity-animated blob planes; fake expensive sims by baking them into vertex-animation textures (Lusion's cloth: positions + normals in two PNGs).

Text strategy: long-form/readable content belongs in HTML overlay (or drei <Html>) — crisp at any DPR, selectable, accessible, SEO-visible; accept that it can't be occluded. Text that must live inside the scene (occluded, lit, on surfaces) uses troika-three-text — SDF glyphs generated in a web worker, no frame drops, crisp when scaled. Never TextGeometry for UI (polygon explosion) and never low-res canvas textures for paragraphs. In-scene screens: either a designed static texture + invisible raycast hitboxes (Jesse) or a real iframe composited via CSS3DRenderer for actual interactivity (Henry).

Performance tiering with hysteresis: clamp dpr={[1, 2]} (Codrops demo went further: 1.0 desktop / 1.5 mobile max); use drei PerformanceMonitor with bounds and flipflops to step DPR/effects down AND up gradually (e.g. setDpr(0.5 + 1.5 * factor)) without visible ping-ponging; run a device benchmark at load and pre-disable reflections, video textures, and bloom on weak hardware targeting a floor (~45fps, Jesse). Budget assets: Draco/gltfjsx -S -T (50-90% size reduction), power-of-two KTX2 textures, instancing for repeated meshes, physics stepped at 1/30 with primitive colliders — Bruno shipped a whole world in 2.8 MB, Codrops' full scene in 2.1 MB.

Sound design that doesn't annoy: Howler.js, started only after the user gesture, with a visible always-reachable mute toggle (persist the choice). Kill repetition — pool 3-5 variants of each SFX, randomize playback rate, scale volume by physical intensity (Bruno scales collision volume by impact velocity). Ambient loop + interaction ticks is enough; music is optional and default-low.

Microinteraction floor: every raycast-hoverable object gets a hover response (scale pulse, outline, cursor swap to pointer) within one frame; springy secondary motion on moving objects (Bruno's antenna lags against acceleration) sells physicality; zero linear tweens and zero instant camera cuts anywhere; idle ambient motion (butterflies, steam, flicker — Jordan Breton) so a motionless user still sees a living scene.

Mobile is a redesign, not a degradation: replace desktop input with purpose-built touch UI (Bruno added a joystick + buttons, breaking his own 'no interface' rule because mobile demanded it), drop reflections/bloom/video textures, clamp DPR harder, and if the experience can't survive — ship a deliberate 2D/scroll fallback plus a visible 'skip to plain site' escape hatch and a WebGL-unsupported fallback page.
half_baked_pitfalls: Default OrbitControls, untouched: no damping, no polar-angle or distance clamps, pan enabled — the visitor immediately looks under the floor, zooms inside the model's head, or strands the camera in the void. Free 6-DOF orbit around a portfolio is an unauthored, uncomposable camera; award sites almost never ship it raw.

Blank white/black screen for 8 seconds, or a progress bar that jumps in chunks and hangs at 100% (the classic default-Unity-loader failure) — visitors bounce before the scene exists. No entrance moment after load: the scene just... appears, fully formed, at frame one.

Unclamped devicePixelRatio: rendering at DPR 3 on a phone or 4K retina, so the very devices most likely to view it get 15fps; or naive FPS-based DPR switching that visibly flip-flops resolution every few seconds because there's no hysteresis.

The unlit gray/black GLTF: MeshStandardMaterial with no environment map and no lights, wrong output color space, model looks nothing like it did in Blender — literally the most common thread on the three.js forum ('Glb model is very dark'). Its sibling: real-time lights and 2048px shadow maps burning frames on a completely static scene that should have been baked.

Z-fighting and depth artifacts: water plane coplanar with the ground shimmering as the camera moves, decals flickering, shadow acne — reads instantly as 'tech demo by someone who didn't look closely'.

Frame drops during the one moment that matters: camera tween or scroll stutters because shaders compile lazily mid-flight (no warm-up/precompile), React state updates inside useFrame trigger re-renders, or the whole postprocessing chain rebuilds on section change.

No mobile plan: instructions say 'use WASD' on a touchscreen, touch events unhandled, HTML overlay overflows the viewport, phone thermal-throttles after 60 seconds. Also no WebGL-failure fallback and no 'skip 3D / view plain site' escape hatch for recruiters in a hurry.
Autoplaying music (which the browser blocks anyway, sometimes leaving the AudioContext permanently suspended) with no visible mute; one collision sound repeated identically 50 times.
Blurry text: paragraphs as TextGeometry or low-res canvas/plane textures instead of HTML overlay or SDF text — unreadable content in a site whose only job is to be read.
A 60 MB payload: uncompressed GLTFs, 4K JPEG textures, no Draco/KTX2 — versus Bruno's entire physics world at 2.8 MB. Long load with no feedback compounds pitfall #2.

Bloom applied to the whole frame (luminanceThreshold left at default ~0.9 under tone mapping) so everything glows milky; effect stacks copy-pasted from examples that serve no concept — chromatic aberration on a minimalist site, film grain on a clean product scene.

The tech demo with no content strategy: impressive scene, but projects/resume are buried three unexplained interactions deep, there's no guidance about what's clickable, and the 3D actively obstructs the hiring manager's 30-second scan. Award winners (cyclist path, room POIs, driving between zones) always author the route through the content.

Housekeeping failures: geometries/textures never disposed on route change (memory climbs until the tab dies), rAF loops still running on hidden tabs, resize handler missing so the canvas distorts on rotate.
notes: Method: web search + primary-source fetches of first-party case studies — Bruno Simon's Medium case study (medium.com/@bruno_simon/bruno-simon-portfolio-case-study-960402cc259b), Jesse Zhou's case study (jesse-zhou.medium.com/jesses-ramen-case-study-77bae77ab5f0), Lusion's Awwwards case study, Henry Heffernan's GitHub (github.com/henryjeff/portfolio-website), R3F scaling-performance docs (r3f.docs.pmnd.rs/advanced/scaling-performance), and Codrops' 2025 'Building Efficient Three.js Scenes' (2.1 MB / 40k tri budget with concrete DPR and gltfjsx numbers). Award context from Awwwards SOTD pages and FWA (Samsy Gen-02 SOTD + Developer Award Oct 2025; Jordan Breton FWA SOTD Oct 2025). The meta-pattern separating premium from amateur: (1) one committed CONCEPT that justifies every effect (CRT shaders because it's a CRT, bloom because it's neon), (2) an AUTHORED camera — every reachable frame is composed, free orbit is never shipped raw, (3) everything expensive is FAKED or PRECOMPUTED offline (baked lighting, matcaps, vertex-animation textures, blob shadows) leaving the frame budget for interaction, (4) loading and entrance are choreographed as the first scene of the experience, and (5) performance is tiered per-device with hysteresis, with mobile treated as its own designed product. Amateur sites are recognizable precisely because defaults are visible: default controls, default loader, default tone-mapped bloom wash, default (missing) mobile story. Caveat: joshuas.world showed a domain-for-sale listing in one search result — the live site may have moved; the Awwwards record is awwwards.com/sites/joshuas-world. Sources also include threejs discourse threads on dark GLTFs and DPR switching, and CSS-Tricks 'Techniques for Rendering Text with WebGL' for the text tradeoffs.
